description: Live TPC-C worker metrics for throughput and performance diagnosis. Not the measurement record; see specification §7.1.

panels.title: How to read this dashboard
panels.description: Scope of the live view versus aggregate.json.

options.content:
Live diagnosis of worker `GET /metrics` (specification §7.1). Ramp-up, measurement, and drain are all included. The measurement record is `aggregate.json`.

**tpmC** is successful New-Order transactions per minute across the selected workers. Test-logic rollbacks count as success. A New-Order rollback share near 1% is the unused-item path, not a failure.

**Within bound** is the share of successes with response time ≤ 5s (New-Order, Payment, Order-Status, Delivery) or ≤ 20s (Stock-Level), from the exact histogram edges. Yellow at 90% and green at 95% are guides for Clause 5.2.5.7. `consolidate` decides `latency_constraints_ok`.

**Breakdown type** filters latency, errors, retries, rollbacks, and client waits. It does not filter this strip, tpmC, the mix, inflight, or per-worker throughput.

Scrape with `mind-tpcc prometheus-config` (job `portable-tpcc`, 15s). Each query Min step is 15s, so `$__rate_interval` covers at least four scrapes. Time is UTC. Colors are diagnostic guides, not alert rules and not an official TPC-C verdict.

panels.title: New-Order tpmC
panels.description: Successful New-Order transactions per minute, summed across the selected workers, including test-logic rollbacks. The rate window is $__rate_interval (at least 60s when the scrape interval is 15s). Not filtered by Breakdown type.

panels.title: Workers down
panels.description: Scrape targets in the current profile, DBMS, and worker filters whose up is 0. 0 means every selected target is up. n/a means Prometheus has no up series for this job yet. A worker lost during measurement fails the run; this panel is only the live signal.

panels.title: Failure ratio
panels.description: Share of completed transactions with result=failure. Test-logic rollbacks stay in result=success and are not counted here. Yellow at 0.1%, red at 1%. All transaction types.

panels.title: Retries per completion
panels.description: Retry increments divided by completed transactions. One transaction can retry more than once, so the value can exceed 1. Yellow at 0.01, red at 0.1. All transaction types.

panels.title: New-Order rollback ratio
panels.description: Test-logic rollbacks divided by successful New-Order. About 1% is the unused-item path. Yellow above 2%, red above 5%. This is not the failure ratio.

panels.title: Inflight
panels.description: Transactions in flight at scrape time, summed across the selected workers. This is a gauge, not a rate. Compare it with max_inflight times the worker count. If it stays near the scheduler thread count while max_inflight is higher, scheduler threads are blocked inside transaction work.

panels.title: New-Order tpmC over time
panels.description: Same formula as the stat: sum of the successful New-Order rate, times 60. Includes ramp-up and drain, so do not copy this number into a result report.

panels.title: Success rate by type
panels.description: Completed successes per second. Filtered by Breakdown type. The mix row below is the view that keeps the small transaction types readable, and it ignores Breakdown type.

panels.title: Transaction mix
panels.description: Each type's share of all successes. Always all five types; Breakdown type does not apply. Payment, Order-Status, Delivery, and Stock-Level have Clause 5.2.3 minima, drawn as the stats underneath. New-Order has no minimum. This is the live mix, not the launch-parameter check.

panels.title: New-Order share
panels.description: Share of successes that are New-Order. Clause 5.2.3 sets no minimum. The built-in mix targets the remainder, about 45%.

panels.title: Payment share
panels.description: Share of successes that are Payment. Clause 5.2.3 minimum is 43%. Red below that, green at or above.

panels.title: Order-Status share
panels.description: Share of successes that are Order-Status. Clause 5.2.3 minimum is 4%.

panels.title: Delivery share
panels.description: Share of successes that are Delivery. Clause 5.2.3 minimum is 4%.

panels.title: Stock-Level share
panels.description: Share of successes that are Stock-Level. Clause 5.2.3 minimum is 4%.

panels.title: New-Order ≤ 5s
panels.description: Share of New-Order successes with response time ≤ 5s. Yellow from 90%, green from 95%. Prometheus 3 stores the worker's integer bucket label with a decimal (5 → 5.0, 20 → 20.0); the selector accepts both forms. This includes ramp-up and drain and is not latency_constraints_ok. Clause 5.2.5.7 is a strict less-than on the measurement-window p90.

panels.title: Payment ≤ 5s
panels.description: Share of Payment successes with response time ≤ 5s. Yellow from 90%, green from 95%. Prometheus 3 stores the worker's integer bucket label with a decimal (5 → 5.0, 20 → 20.0); the selector accepts both forms. This includes ramp-up and drain and is not latency_constraints_ok. Clause 5.2.5.7 is a strict less-than on the measurement-window p90.

panels.title: Order-Status ≤ 5s
panels.description: Share of Order-Status successes with response time ≤ 5s. Yellow from 90%, green from 95%. Prometheus 3 stores the worker's integer bucket label with a decimal (5 → 5.0, 20 → 20.0); the selector accepts both forms. This includes ramp-up and drain and is not latency_constraints_ok. Clause 5.2.5.7 is a strict less-than on the measurement-window p90.

panels.title: Delivery ≤ 5s
panels.description: Share of Delivery successes with response time ≤ 5s. Yellow from 90%, green from 95%. Prometheus 3 stores the worker's integer bucket label with a decimal (5 → 5.0, 20 → 20.0); the selector accepts both forms. This includes ramp-up and drain and is not latency_constraints_ok. Clause 5.2.5.7 is a strict less-than on the measurement-window p90.

panels.title: Stock-Level ≤ 20s
panels.description: Share of Stock-Level successes with response time ≤ 20s. Yellow from 90%, green from 95%. Prometheus 3 stores the worker's integer bucket label with a decimal (5 → 5.0, 20 → 20.0); the selector accepts both forms. This includes ramp-up and drain and is not latency_constraints_ok. Clause 5.2.5.7 is a strict less-than on the measurement-window p90.

panels.title: Success p50
panels.description: Success p50 of client response time for result=success (includes test-logic rollbacks). histogram_quantile after summing bucket rates across the selected workers. Do not read this as the consolidate percentile: the Prometheus buckets are coarse, and the series include ramp-up and drain.

panels.title: Success p90
panels.description: Success p90 of client response time for result=success (includes test-logic rollbacks). histogram_quantile after summing bucket rates across the selected workers. Do not read this as the consolidate percentile: the Prometheus buckets are coarse, and the series include ramp-up and drain.

panels.title: Success p99
panels.description: Success p99 of client response time for result=success (includes test-logic rollbacks). histogram_quantile after summing bucket rates across the selected workers. Do not read this as the consolidate percentile: the Prometheus buckets are coarse, and the series include ramp-up and drain.

panels.title: Success mean
panels.description: Mean success response time: rate of the histogram sum divided by rate of the count, per type. Same population and window as the percentile panels.

panels.title: Failure p90
panels.description: p90 client response time of result=failure. Empty when the selected types have no failures in the window. A short failure p90 with a high failure ratio points at fast rejects; a long one points at timeouts.

panels.title: Failure ratio by type
panels.description: result=failure over all completions of that type. Rollbacks are not in the numerator. Filtered by Breakdown type.

panels.title: Retry rate by type
panels.description: Retryable-error retries per second. This counts attempts that were retried, not failed transactions. Pair with retry-backoff wait.

panels.title: Rollback rate by type
panels.description: Test-logic rollbacks per second. These completions are also successes and count toward tpmC. New-Order should sit near 1% of its success rate; other types are normally zero.

panels.title: Inflight by worker
panels.description: Gauge at scrape time. Total is the same sum as the health-strip stat. A worker whose inflight sits on a low plateau while others climb is not taking its share of concurrency.

panels.title: Admission wait
panels.description: Time a terminal waited for an inflight slot before the transaction started. Every completion is a sample, including zeros. A rising p90 means terminals are queueing on max_inflight. Solid lines are p90, dashed lines are the mean.

panels.title: Session-pool wait
panels.description: Time spent waiting for a DBMS connection or session. Every completion is a sample, including zeros. A rising p90 means the pool is saturated. Pool size is min(terminals, max_inflight). Solid lines are p90, dashed lines are the mean.

panels.title: Retry-backoff wait
panels.description: Time spent in retry backoff after retryable errors. Every completion is a sample, including zeros. A rising p90 means retries are adding latency. Pair with the retry rate. Solid lines are p90, dashed lines are the mean.

panels.title: New-Order tpmC by worker
panels.description: Successful New-Order per minute for each selected worker. A worker far below the others is a skew signal. The next panel divides each worker by the median.

panels.title: Worker tpmC / median
panels.description: Each worker's New-Order tpmC divided by the median of the selected workers. The lines at 0.9 and 1.0 are visual guides for skew, not a conformance limit. n/a while every selected rate is zero.

panels.title: New-Order success p90 by worker
panels.description: p90 success response time of New-Order on each worker. The line at 5s is the Clause 5.2.5.7 bound for this type. The bucket is coarse, so also use the New-Order ≤ 5s stat.

panels.title: Scrape up
panels.description: Prometheus up for the selected targets. 0 means the scrape failed and the worker is still in the scrape config. A gap means the target disappeared. Loss of a worker during measurement fails the run.
